rationale.conceptual: The method is an established DFT slab relaxation with a specific interface model (C–O–Al bonding). While not novel, it requires careful construction of slab models, choice of pseudopotentials, convergence tests, and computation of adhesion energy and surface relaxation. This goes beyond a trivial textbook operation but does not involve a new algorithm. It sits at the level of a non-trivial but documented multi-component method.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves building slab models, running two separate DFT relaxations (bare surface and interface), and post-processing to extract distances, energies, and contractions. Setting up Quantum ESPRESSO, handling pseudopotentials, ensuring force convergence, and correctly computing adhesion energy constitute a fragile multi-tool orchestration with several load-bearing handoffs. It is a longer pipeline than a simple script and requires managing computational workflow.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires performing standard DFT slab calculations to reproduce interface geometry and adhesion energy. The conceptual difficulty is moderate (standard method, careful convergence), and execution involves multi-step pipeline with DFT code setup and post-processing.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The DFT relaxations involve small slabs (tens of atoms) and use plane-wave codes. A single multi-core CPU with ~16 GB RAM is sufficient; no GPU is required. The only external data is the bulk crystal structure of α-Al₂O₃, which is a tiny input file (<10 KB).
